claims.text: The initial alloy is an as-cast, non-equilibrium Mg-containing high-entropy alloy with density below 6 g/cm3.
The initial alloy has a relatively homogeneous matrix containing dissolved Mg.
Early-stage intermetallic compounds are present in the initial as-cast alloy.
Thermal aging causes decomposition of the supersaturated matrix.
Thermal aging forms Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates form primarily at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
At high temperature, the Mg-rich precipitates oxidize preferentially.
Preferential oxidation of Mg-rich precipitates nucleates a continuous MgO-rich surface scale.
The MgO-rich scale is protective and improves high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast alloy.
An electrochemical-potential difference exists between Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates and the surrounding matrix.
The potential difference between precipitates and matrix establishes local galvanic cells.
The resulting galvanic cells alter corrosion pathways and intensify localized corrosion in susceptible microregions.
The aged alloy will exhibit more localized attack at intermetallic/matrix interfaces than the as-cast baseline.
The proposed evolution requires sufficient Mg in the non-equilibrium initial microstructure to drive intermetallic formation during thermal exposure.
Alternative processing routes or vastly different Mg contents may produce different evolution and performance.
